question: The spine was proved on a Forwarding booking. Does the rest of the business work — contracts, and the other service lines?
framing: Forwarding is the smallest service line on dev (20 bookings). Brokerage carries 142 and Trucking 81. Every e2e test and manual pass so far has exercised 8% of the traffic.

findings.title: The other service lines are wired — Trucking is untested, not broken
findings.evidence: Every service line has its own detail component wiring the same UnifiedBillingsTab / UnifiedExpensesTab / UnifiedInvoicesTab / UnifiedCollectionsTab with a per-line permission door: BrokerageBookingDetails, TruckingBookingDetails:400, MarineInsuranceBookingDetails, OthersBookingDetails, forwarding/ForwardingBookingDetails.
findings.conclusion: Trucking's 0 billing lines and 0 e-vouchers are missing test coverage, not a missing feature. Stated explicitly because the empty columns invite the opposite conclusion.

findings.title: The type filter hides every spot quotation
findings.cause: The filter offers All Types / Project / Contract. 'Contract' keeps quotation_type === 'contract'; 'Project' keeps !quotation_type || === 'project'. The third live value, 'spot', matches neither branch.
findings.effect: All 18 spot quotations are reachable only on 'All Types'. Narrowing to either named type drops them with no indication.

findings.title: Contract expiry is a label nobody flips
findings.cause: No trigger on quotations touches contract status; pg_cron is not installed. detect_active_contracts_for_customer gates on contract_status in ('Active','Expiring') and never compares a date. fetchFullContract and CreateBookingFromContractPanel add no validity check.

measured.live_case: CQ2605251999 — contract_end_date 2026-05-01, contract_status 'Active', still returned by the booking-detection RPC on 2026-08-06

findings.note: ContractsList:593 renders 'Expired' when daysRemaining <= 0, but that is a display string only; the stored status is unchanged and the RPC reads the stored status.

findings.title: get_contract_for_booking ignores the visibility dial
findings.cause: The by-id RPC filters only on quotation_type='contract' after a wide capability gate, then returns to_jsonb of the entire row. No customer scoping, no department check, no visibility dial.
findings.gate: current_user_can_detect_contracts() passes on any of pricing_quotations:view, pricing_contracts:view, bd_contracts:view, bd_inquiries:view, current_user_can_act_on_booking('view'), acct_bookings:view — roughly everyone in BD, Pricing, Ops or Accounting.
findings.explicitly_not_the_finding: Buying-price exposure to internal staff is by design — internal financials are deliberately not role-gated per Marcus's standing instruction. The finding is that a user whose visibility dial is 'own' can read any contract in the system by id, which is what migration 217 established the dial to prevent.
findings.contrast: The sibling RPC detect_active_contracts_for_customer IS customer-scoped and returns header fields only. The call-site comment describes that behaviour; the by-id function has neither property.

findings.title: The per-booking Financials tab is granted to 3 of 60 users
declared_correctly_in: the can() calls in each BookingDetails component
findings.note: ops_trucking_financials_tab does not appear as a key in permission_overrides or access_profiles at all.
findings.effect: Nobody — including Accounting — can open per-booking financials for Trucking (81 bookings), Marine Insurance or Others. Consistent with the standing doctrine that a tab is invisible until checked in the Access Configuration matrix.

findings.title: The catalog doctrine is enforced by convention only
findings.doctrine: CLAUDE.md, non-negotiable: no billing_line_items or evoucher_line_items insert may omit catalog_item_id; every catalog write must include catalog_snapshot from buildCatalogSnapshot().
findings.why_it_matters: The catalog is the mechanism that makes revenue and cost comparable across service lines. Two thirds of billing rows sit outside it.

verdict: Contracts are the weakest area QA has examined — not because the code is bad, but because the parts meant to be automatic are manual. A contract expires when someone changes a dropdown. A catalog rule holds when someone remembers it. A tab becomes visible when someone ticks a box, and for three service lines nobody did.
recommended_order: R2 — one date comparison in detect_active_contracts_for_customer plus a status backfill; the one where a wrong answer holds the company to a rate it no longer honours
R5 — two NOT NULL constraints, AFTER a decision on the 197 existing violating rows (no data touched)
R3 — a scoping clause on get_contract_for_booking
R1 — one line in the list filter
R4 — an Access Configuration matrix change, not code
